title: A Ember for the Oath Again
premise: Bram Eastwick, a beast-speaker who hides his forbidden gift even from the smugglers he guides through the Thornfell mountains, is pressed into service by a dying stranger bearing a map to the Hollow Crown — the ancient binding that keeps a thing of ash and hunger wearing the king's face. Hunted by crown wardens and the smugglers' own betrayed guild, Bram gathers an unlikely found family: a disgraced oath-keeper, a memory-thief girl, and a wolf who speaks back. As winter seals the passes, they learn the map's true purpose: not to steal the crown, but to unbind the king from it before the long winter finishes falling and the thing beneath wakes fully. In the end Bram must surrender his most guarded secret — his voice — to speak the unbinding, trading a piece of his own memory of the people he loves for the king's freedom.
about_author: Ada Reyes is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six winters in mountain country and now writes fantasy about the debts we owe strangers. She lives somewhere high and cold, keeping careful notes on what the ravens say.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A routine run through Thornfell goes wrong when Bram's quiet word to a mule saves the caravan from a rockslide, nearly exposing his gift to the guild master Vess. He covers, but she watches him now. Emotional beat: the cost of hiding — safety bought with silence.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At a frozen river crossing, a dying man in torn royal livery staggers out of the snow and presses a wax-sealed map into Bram's hands, whispering 'the king is not the king' before the ice takes him. Emotional beat: dread and unwanted inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Ravens Knew
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram questions the crows along the pass; their scattered images show the stranger fleeing crown wardens. Vess demands the map as guild property. Bram lies for the first time outright. Emotional beat: the point of no return, chosen alone.

chapters.title: The Oath-Keeper's Cell
chapters.summary: Sera's POV (introduced). Sera Vance, a disgraced oath-keeper rotting in a border garrison, recognizes the dead man's seal when Bram comes asking questions. She breaks them both out rather than let the seal be buried. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's honor.

chapters.title: Wardens on the White Road
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Crown wardens led by Captain Ilse Dorn hunt them down the high road; Bram speaks a herd of goats into stampeding the patrol. Sera sees the gift and says nothing. Emotional beat: terror of being seen, and the strange relief after.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Sold Yesterday
chapters.summary: Nix's POV (introduced). In the market town of Lowbridge, Nix, a memory-thief child, tries to pickpocket Bram and instead tastes a fragment of his memory of the dying stranger. Frightened and fascinated, she follows them out of town. Emotional beat: loneliness finding its shape.

chapters.title: Vess's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The guild master sells Bram's route and description to Captain Dorn, weighing old affection against gold and fear. She tells herself it's justice for his theft. Emotional beat: betrayal rationalized, guilt already taking root.

chapters.title: The Map That Reads Back
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Camped in a shepherd's ruin, the three decode the map: it shows the Hollow Crown beneath Greywatch Keep, and the ink shifts to reflect each reader's memories. Nix touches it and screams. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror at what the crown truly is.

chapters.title: Winter Closes the Passes
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The first true blizzard traps them in a cave with a wounded wolf Bram coaxes back from death — and the wolf answers him aloud, naming itself Ash. Found family solidifies around a fire. Emotional beat: warmth against the falling dark.

chapters.title: Dorn's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dorn's POV. The warden captain captures Vess and offers her amnesty for Bram's head; flashbacks reveal Dorn once served the real king and suspects the truth of the crown. Emotional beat: a hunter who no longer believes in her hunt.

chapters.title: Lowbridge Burns
chapters.summary: Nix's POV. Wardens torch Lowbridge hunting them; Nix steals a warden's memory to buy escape and carries his dying terror home with her. Bram chooses to save townsfolk over the map, losing half a day. Emotional beat: the first price of doing right outside the law.

chapters.title: The Guild's Judgment
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Vess corners Bram at the smugglers' shrine, blade drawn, but cannot strike when he offers his life freely and names her the sister she once was. She lets them go and turns on Dorn instead. Emotional beat: mercy as rebellion.

chapters.title: Greywatch in the Snow
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The company reaches Greywatch Keep disguised as corpse-haulers; inside, they see the king — young-eyed, hollow, mouthing help me between public smiles. Sera's broken oath rekindles. Emotional beat: hope arriving dressed as despair.

chapters.title: The Thing Beneath the Crown
chapters.summary: Ash's POV (the wolf). Through beast-speech, Ash reveals the crown is a cage forged by the first oath-keepers, and the thing inside has been eating the king's winters one by one. Emotional beat: myth made intimate; the scale of the stakes lands.

chapters.title: Nix's Price
chapters.summary: Nix's POV. To reach the vault, Nix must steal the gatekeeper's memory wholesale — risking losing her own name in the exchange. She does it, and for one terrible hour forgets Bram and Sera entirely. Emotional beat: sacrifice measured in selfhood.

chapters.title: Captain Dorn's Choice
chapters.summary: Dorn's POV. Dorn finds them in the vault corridor, sword raised — then kneels, giving them her key and her confession: she swore her oath to the man, not the mask. Emotional beat: the law bending toward justice.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. In the vault beneath Greywatch, Sera restores her oath aloud while Bram begins the speaking; the crown-thing fights back with stolen memories, showing Bram his mother abandoning him. Emotional beat: the climax's threshold — love weaponized against them.

chapters.title: Every Voice but His Own
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The rite requires a voice the crown has never heard; Bram gives it his gift, calling every creature in Greywatch to speak the unbinding with him — mules, ravens, wolves, the keep's dying hounds. Emotional beat: the hidden self finally spent, gloriously.

chapters.title: The King in the Ash
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The crown shatters; the thing dissolves into drifting ash, and the king collapses into Bram's arms, weeping, whole, remembering nothing of his lost years. Outside, the unnatural winter breaks. Emotional beat: release after unbearable tension.

chapters.title: What Bram Forgot
chapters.summary: Nix's POV. The rite took its toll: Bram cannot remember his mother's face or the sound of Vess's laugh. Nix quietly returns a stolen shard of his memory she'd kept, the first thing she's ever given back. Emotional beat: grief braided with grace.

chapters.title: Oaths Rewritten
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The restored king pardons the smugglers and asks Sera to rebuild the oath-keepers; Dorn takes the grey cloak beside her. Vess arrives under truce, ledger burned, and offers Bram his routes back. Emotional beat: institutions remade by the people outside them.

chapters.title: An Ember for the Road
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Spring thaws Thornfell. Bram, voice quieter now but still heard by beasts, walks the high road with Ash at his side, Nix chattering, carrying an ember from the shattered crown to light the way for whoever needs it next. Emotional beat: earned peace, open horizon.
